title: Bamboo Weaving: An Ancient Craft Weaves a New Future
title_zh: 竹编：古老手艺编织新未来
intro_zh: 本文约980词，目标900词，新词6个，理解目标90%。

paragraphs.en: In many villages across China, a familiar sound used to echo through the morning air: the soft crackle of bamboo strips being bent and shaped by skilled hands. This was the sound of bamboo weaving, one of the oldest crafts in Chinese culture. For centuries, bamboo baskets, trays, and furniture were essential parts of daily life. Yet today, this ancient handicraft faces a serious challenge. As plastic products became cheap and widely available, the demand for handwoven bamboo items dropped sharply. Many young people left rural areas for city jobs, leaving fewer hands to carry on the tradition. However, a new wave of interest is emerging, driven by a new generation of artisans who are giving bamboo weaving a fresh and exciting future.
paragraphs.zh: 在中国许多村庄，过去常常有一种熟悉的声音在晨空中回荡：富有技巧的双手弯曲和塑造竹条时发出的轻柔噼啪声。这就是竹编的声音，竹编是中华文化中最古老的手工艺之一。几个世纪以来，竹篮、竹盘和竹家具是日常生活的必需品。然而今天，这门古老的手艺面临严峻挑战。随着塑料产品变得便宜且普及，手编竹制品的需求大幅下降。许多年轻人离开农村到城市工作，留下越来越少的人来延续这一传统。不过，一股新的兴趣浪潮正在兴起，由新一代工匠推动，他们为竹编注入了新鲜而激动人心的未来。

paragraphs.en: Bamboo weaving is not just a simple handicraft; it is a perfect combination of nature and human creativity. Bamboo is an amazing material that grows quickly and is both strong and flexible. Artisans choose the right type of bamboo for each product, often soaking and splitting the stalks into thin, even strips. The weaving process demands great patience and skill. Some of the weaving techniques are so intricate that they require years of practice to master. A simple basket may take several hours, while a complex piece of furniture might need weeks of careful work. Many techniques have been passed down from generation to generation, with each region developing its own unique styles and patterns.
paragraphs.zh: 竹编不仅仅是一项简单的手工活；它是自然与人类创造力的完美结合。竹子是一种神奇的材料，生长迅速，既坚固又有韧性。工匠们为每件产品选择合适的竹子，通常要浸泡并把竹茎劈成细而均匀的条。编织过程需要极大的耐心和技巧。有些编织技法非常复杂精细，需要多年练习才能掌握。一个简单的篮子可能需要几个小时，而一件复杂的家具可能需数周的精心工作。许多技法代代相传，每个地区都发展出独特的风格和图案。

paragraphs.en: The craft has deep roots in Chinese culture. Archaeologists have found bamboo items dating back more than 7,000 years, showing how long this material has been part of human life. In ancient times, bamboo was used for everything from writing slips to building materials, and woven objects were valued for their durability and beauty. Traditional bamboo baskets were used to collect tea leaves, carry goods, and store grain. Woven bamboo mats provided cool, comfortable sleeping surfaces in summer. However, the younger generation often sees these products as old-fashioned and cheap, which has made it difficult for the craft to survive in a modern consumer society.
paragraphs.zh: 这门手艺深深植根于中华文化。考古学家发现了距今超过7000年的竹制品，显示出这种材料在人类生活中存在了多么久远。在古代，竹子被用于从书写简到建筑材料等各种方面，而编织物因其耐用和美观而备受珍视。传统竹篮被用来采茶叶、运货物、存粮食。编织的竹席在夏天提供凉爽舒适的睡眠表面。然而，年轻一代常常认为这些产品过时且廉价，这使得这门手艺在现代消费社会中难以生存。

paragraphs.en: One major problem is the lack of new apprentices. In the past, young people often learned the skill from their parents or grandparents. With the rapid development of cities, many prefer to work in factories or offices where they can earn a more stable income. Consequently, the average age of bamboo weavers is rising, and many traditional techniques are now endangered as fewer people are learning them. According to a survey from 2019, about one-third of traditional handicrafts in China are at risk of being lost. To address this issue, local governments and cultural organizations have started promoting these crafts. They offer free training classes, provide subsidies to artisans, and organize exhibitions to increase awareness. These measures help, but they are often too small to stop the decline completely.
paragraphs.zh: 一个主要问题是缺乏新学徒。过去，年轻人经常从父母或祖父母那里学习这门技艺。随着城市的迅速发展，许多人更愿意在工厂或办公室工作，这样可以获得更稳定的收入。因此，竹编匠人的平均年龄在上升，许多传统技法因为学习的人越来越少而濒危。根据2019年的一项调查，中国大约三分之一的传统手工艺面临失传风险。为了解决这个问题，地方政府和文化组织开始推广这些工艺。他们提供免费培训班，向工匠提供补贴，并组织展览以提升意识。这些措施有帮助，但往往规模太小，无法完全阻止衰落。

paragraphs.en: Fortunately, a new generation of craftspeople is changing the story. Many young designers and artists have a growing interest in handmade objects and the stories behind them. They see bamboo weaving as a meaningful way to connect with Chinese tradition and to create environmentally friendly products for a worried planet. One such person is Wang Fang, a 28-year-old designer from Anhui province. After studying industrial design in Shanghai, she decided to return to her hometown to learn bamboo weaving from her uncle, who had practiced the craft for over 40 years. At first, Wang found the work extremely difficult and her hands often hurt. But she persisted, believing that she could adapt the ancient skill for modern life. She began to design new products, such as lampshades and laptop stands, that combine traditional weaving with contemporary needs.
paragraphs.zh: 幸运的是，新一代的工匠正在改变这个局面。许多年轻设计师和艺术家对手工制品及其背后的故事越来越感兴趣。他们把竹编视为连接中华传统和为地球创造环保产品的有意义方式。其中一位是来自安徽的28岁设计师王芳。在上海学习工业设计后，她决定回到家乡，向有40多年手艺的叔叔学习竹编。起初，王芳觉得这项工作极其困难，她的手经常受伤。但她坚持了下来，相信自己能够使这门古老技艺适应现代生活。她开始设计新产品，如灯罩和笔记本电脑支架，将传统编织与现代需求相结合。

paragraphs.en: Wang's initiative is part of a broader movement. Online platforms, especially short-video apps like Douyin, have become powerful tools for promoting traditional crafts. Weavers now film short videos showing their hands creating beautiful patterns, and these videos often receive millions of views. Through these videos, viewers discover the complexity and beauty of bamboo weaving, and some become interested in buying handmade items or even learning the craft themselves. E-commerce has also opened new markets, allowing artisans to sell their products directly to customers across the country and even abroad. A beautifully woven bamboo basket can now be sold online for several hundred yuan, which provides a much better income than selling to local markets.
paragraphs.zh: 王芳的行动是更广泛运动的一部分。在线平台，尤其是像抖音这样的短视频应用，已经成为推广传统手艺的强大工具。编织者们现在拍摄短视频，展示他们的双手制作精美图案，这些视频常常获得数百万次观看。通过这些视频，观众发现了竹编的复杂性和美感，有些人开始对购买手工艺品甚至亲自学习这门手艺产生兴趣。电子商务还打开了新市场，让工匠可以直接向全国各地乃至国外的客户销售他们的产品。一个编织精美的竹篮现在可以在网上卖到几百元，这比卖给当地市场提供了更好的收入。

paragraphs.en: Still, challenges remain. The attention from short videos can be short-lived, and making a living solely from bamboo weaving is not easy for everyone. There is also a risk that mass production might dilute the traditional quality. To ensure the revival lasts, some experts suggest that schools should include traditional crafts in their art courses. This would help more young people understand and appreciate this tradition. In addition, design competitions and cultural events can inspire new ideas. One promising development is the growing interest in eco-friendly products. Because bamboo is a renewable resource and products are biodegradable, bamboo weaving fits perfectly with the global push for sustainability. Bamboo is a sustainable material, and it naturally fits this trend. This connection could attract more consumers and keep the craft alive for future generations.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管如此，挑战仍然存在。短视频带来的关注可能是短暂的，而且仅仅靠竹编谋生对每个人都不容易。还有一种风险是，大规模生产可能会削弱传统品质。为了确保持续复兴，一些专家建议学校应在艺术课程中加入传统手工艺的内容。这将帮助更多年轻人理解并欣赏这一传统。此外，设计比赛和文化活动可以激发新想法。一个令人鼓舞的发展是人们对环保产品日益增长的兴趣。由于竹子是可再生资源，产品可生物降解，竹编完美契合了全球对可持续发展的追求。竹子是一种可持续材料，自然契合这一趋势。这种联系可以吸引更多消费者，让这门手艺在未来世代中持续生存。

paragraphs.en: In the end, bamboo weaving is more than just a way to make objects. It carries the memory of a civilization, the wisdom of our ancestors, and a deep respect for nature. The revival of this craft is not about turning back the clock; it is about weaving old threads into new patterns. With the efforts of passionate individuals, supportive policies, and modern technology, traditional craftsmanship can find a place in our modern world. As Wang Fang says, 'Every bamboo strip has a story. When we weave, we tell that story — and we also write a new one.' It is this human touch that gives the ancient craft its lasting charm and ensures it will not be forgotten. Indeed, bamboo weaving is a living heritage that connects us to our ancestors and enriches our future.
paragraphs.zh: 最终，竹编不仅仅是制造物品的一种方式。它承载着一个文明的记忆、我们祖先的智慧，以及对自然的深深敬意。这门手艺的复兴不是要逆转时光；而是把旧线编织成新图案。在充满热情的个体、支持性的政策和现代科技的努力下，传统手工艺可以在我们的现代世界中找到一席之地。正如王芳所说，“每一根竹条都有一个故事。当我们编织时，我们在讲述那个故事——同时也在书写一个新的故事。”正是这种人文触感赋予了古老手艺持久的魅力，并确保它不会被遗忘。的确，竹编是一种鲜活的遗产，将我们与祖先相连，并丰富我们的未来。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: The history of bamboo weaving in China.
The challenges and revival of bamboo weaving.
questions.explain: 主旨题。文章先讲竹编的衰落，再讲新一代的努力和新机遇，所以主旨是竹编面临的挑战和复兴。

questions.q: According to the passage, which of the following is a reason for the decline of bamboo weaving?
options: The high cost of bamboo materials.
The difficulty of the craft itself.
questions.explain: 细节题。文章第一段提到'As plastic products became cheap and widely available, the demand for handwoven bamboo items dropped sharply.' 因此塑料产品的普及是原因。

questions.q: What can be inferred about Wang Fang?
options: She learned bamboo weaving from her grandfather.
She is a traditional weaver without modern education.
She is trying to combine tradition with modern design.
She believes bamboo weaving will disappear soon.
questions.explain: 推断题。根据她设计新产品如灯罩和电脑支架，可推断她努力将传统与现代结合。

questions.q: The word 'dilute' in paragraph 7 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 词义题。dilute原意'稀释'，此处'大规模生产可能会削弱传统品质'，所以与weaken同义。
